newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Bid by Triplex boosts William Cook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bid by Triplex boosts William Cook.

text.p: British engineering group Triplex Lloyd said on Friday it was making a 57.7 million pounds ($96.10 million) cash and shares offer for William Cook Plc, sending stock in the steel company soaring.

"It is a very logical move for us," Triplex group chief executive Graham Lockyer told Reuters in an interview. "We have done our homework, it (William Cook) is fully valued and we will do what needs to be done to achieve our goal."
The bid was warmly received by the city, which pushed shares in William Cook 77-1/2 pence higher to 318 pence by 1045 GMT. Triplex Lloyd shares moved three pence higher to 210 pence.

Triplex said the offer valued each William Cook share at 309 pence and would be made on the basis of seven new Triplex Lloyd shares and 1350 pence in cash for every nine William Cook shares. William Cook was not immediately available for comment.
The offer represents a 30 percent premium to William Cook's share price of 240.5 pence at the close on November 14.

Triplex Lloyd said its proposed acquisition should add some 1.5 million pounds to profits on an annualised basis. It said on November 11 it had increased half year pretax profits to 6.2 million pounds from 3.4 million previously.
The profit increase will come from the ability to generate opportunities from sales and marketing, particularly in the petrochemical markets, the company said in a statement.
"Our best judgement is that it (the acquisition) will be earnings enhancing," said Lockyer.
"William Cook shareholders are suffering from their management's loss of ambition and its failure to pursue new growth opportunities successfully," he said.
The enlarged group will sell cast products to customers in a broad range of industries in Europe, North America and Asia, said Triplex Lloyd.
William Cook shareholders will also be offered a fully underwritten cash alternative of 295p per William Cook Share. There is also a share election and a loan note alternative.

Triplex Lloyd said full acceptance of the offer would involve issuing around 14.5 million new shares, representing around 18 percent of its enlarged share capital. It would also require a cash payment of 28 million pounds.
